summaries.summary: Electrical engineering is an engineering discipline concerned with the study, design, and application of equipment, devices, and systems that use electricity, electronics, and electromagnetism. It emerged as an identifiable occupation in the latter half of the 19th century after the commercialization of the electric telegraph, the telephone, and electrical power generation, distribution, and use. The field is the parent discipline for a range of subfields, including telecommunications, computer engineering, power systems, control, signal processing, and photonics. Practitioners work across scales from microelectronic circuits and integrated devices to continent-spanning power grids and communication networks. In the Library of Congress Classification, electrical engineering, electronics, and nuclear engineering are grouped under class TK.

summaries.summary: Telecommunications engineering is a subfield of electrical engineering which seeks to design and devise systems of communication at a distance. The work ranges from basic circuit design to strategic mass developments. A telecommunication engineer is responsible for designing and overseeing the installation of telecommunications equipment and facilities, such as complex electronic switching systems, optical fiber cabling, IP networks, and microwave transmission systems. The discipline also overlaps with broadcast engineering. Its subject matter—telephony, radio, fiber-optic and IP networks, and spectrum use—is coordinated internationally by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), described as "the United Nations specialized agency for digital technologies (ICTs)."

summaries.summary: Computer engineering is a branch of engineering specialized in developing computer hardware and software. As an engineering discipline at the interface of electrical engineering and computing, it spans digital-logic and circuit design, processor and embedded-system architecture, and the system software that runs on that hardware, distinguishing it from computer science as a practice rooted in engineering design. The professional community is served by the IEEE Computer Society, which describes itself as "Engaging computer engineers, scientists, academia, and industry professionals from all areas of computing," and which sets standards and curricula spanning both hardware and software concepts. Computer engineers work on the design and integration of computing systems rather than on abstract computation alone.

summaries.summary: Photonics is the science and engineering of generating, detecting, and manipulating light in the form of photons—through emission, transmission, modulation, signal processing, switching, amplification, and sensing. It underpins technologies such as lasers, optical fibers and optical communication, photodetectors, displays, and optical sensing. Photonics coexists with optics; there is no widespread agreement on a sharp boundary between the two, and the term gained currency as photon-based devices and systems matured. The discipline is represented by professional societies including SPIE, "the largest global optics and photonics professional society," and Optica (formerly OSA), "the society dedicated to promoting the generation, application, archiving and dissemination of knowledge in the field."

citations.supports: Definition of photonics in terms of generation/detection/manipulation of light as photons (emission, transmission, modulation, switching, amplification, sensing) and the noted lack of a firm boundary with optics
citations.quote: Photonics is a branch of optics that involves the application of generation, detection, and manipulation of light in the form of photons through emission, transmission, modulation, signal processing, switching, amplification, and sensing. Even though photonics is a commonly used term, there is no widespread agreement on a clear definition of the term or on the difference between photonics and related fields, such as optics.

summaries.summary: Systems engineering is an interdisciplinary field of engineering and engineering management that focuses on how to design, integrate, and manage complex systems over their life cycles. It uses systems-thinking principles to organize the systems engineering body of knowledge, and the resulting engineered system can be defined as a combination of components that work in synergy to collectively perform a useful function. Rather than optimizing parts in isolation, the discipline coordinates requirements, architecture, interfaces, verification, and operations across a system's whole life cycle, from concept through retirement. The international professional society for the discipline is the International Council on Systems Engineering (INCOSE).

citations.supports: Definition as an interdisciplinary field of engineering and engineering management for designing, integrating, and managing complex systems over their life cycles; use of systems-thinking principles; and the synergy-of-components definition of an engineered system
citations.quote: Systems engineering is an interdisciplinary field of engineering and engineering management that focuses on how to design, integrate, and manage complex systems over their life cycles. At its core, systems engineering utilizes systems thinking principles to organize the systems engineering body of knowledge. The individual outcome of such efforts, an engineered system, can be defined as a combination of components that work in synergy to collectively perform a useful function.
